contentBody: **What is an automation workflow in simple terms?**
option.1: A manual checklist that people tick off on paper
option.2: Connected steps that run automatically after a trigger
option.3: A spreadsheet listing all your tasks and their due dates
option.4: A meeting agenda for the whole team to follow each week
answerExplanation: A workflow is "when this happens, do that", with no one doing the steps by hand.

contentBody: **Under n8n's Sustainable Use License, what would need a separate commercial agreement?**
option.1: Self-hosting it on a server for your own team
option.2: Using it for your own internal business tasks
option.3: Reselling it to clients as a hosted service
option.4: Using it for your own personal projects
answerExplanation: Internal and personal use are allowed; reselling n8n as a service is not.

contentBody: **How should n8n be described most accurately in writing?**
option.1: Fair-code: public source code, with some use limits
option.2: Public domain, free for anyone to use for anything
option.3: Fully open source, with no limits at all on any use
option.4: Closed source, with all of its code kept private
answerExplanation: Its source is public but the licence limits commercial reselling, so "fair-code" is the accurate term.

contentBody: **Which of these tasks is the best candidate for automation?**
option.1: Deciding which lead deserves a personal call
option.2: Comforting an upset or angry customer
option.3: Negotiating a discount with a client
option.4: Logging every form entry into a shared sheet
answerExplanation: It has a clear trigger, fixed rules and digital data; the others need judgement or empathy.

contentBody: **What makes a process a good automation candidate in practice?**
option.1: It needs human judgement and empathy every time
option.2: It only happens about once or twice a year
option.3: It follows clear, fixed rules and repeats very often
option.4: It relies on paper records and handwritten forms alone
answerExplanation: Rule-based, digital, frequent work repays the effort of automating it.

contentBody: **In "when this happens, do that," what is the "this happens" part?**
option.1: The action that follows
option.2: The result at the end
option.3: The saved credential login
option.4: The trigger event itself
answerExplanation: The trigger is the event that starts the workflow.

contentBody: **Company rules say customer data must stay on its own servers. Which option leans best?**
option.1: Any vendor-hosted tool online
option.2: Self-hosted n8n on its servers
option.3: A shared public account for everyone
option.4: Email attachments sent around
answerExplanation: Self-hosting keeps the data on servers the company controls.

contentBody: **Which of these processes should stay with a person?**
option.1: Deciding which enquiry gets a personal call back
option.2: Copying form entries into a shared sheet
option.3: Sending a weekly summary email report
option.4: Posting an alert in chat when a payment fails
answerExplanation: Judgement-heavy work stays human; the others follow fixed rules.

contentBody: **Which control runs the whole workflow one time for testing purposes?**
option.1: The Execute workflow button
option.2: The Publish button in the top bar
option.3: The Tidy Up control
option.4: The Zoom to Fit control
answerExplanation: Execute workflow is a manual test run; Publish switches the triggers on.

contentBody: **What starts a workflow running by itself?**
option.1: An action node that sends data to an app
option.2: A parameter on a node
option.3: A data item passed along
option.4: A trigger node waiting for events
answerExplanation: A trigger waits for an event and starts the run; actions follow it.

contentBody: **A node's parameter reads {{ $json.Email }}. What kind of value is it exactly?**
option.1: A fixed, typed-in value
option.2: An expression read from data
option.3: A saved credential login
option.4: A trigger for the workflow
answerExplanation: An expression is looked up from earlier data each time the workflow runs.

contentBody: **A form trigger outputs three items. How many rows does the Append Row node add?**
option.1: Only one row in total
option.2: No rows at all
option.3: Three rows, one per item
option.4: Six rows, two per item
answerExplanation: Most nodes run once per incoming item.

contentBody: **Where exactly does an item's data sit in n8n's internal data structure?**
option.1: Under the key named json
option.2: Under the workflow's title text
option.3: Inside the saved credential login
option.4: Inside the canvas sticky note
answerExplanation: Each item wraps its fields in a json key.

contentBody: **Where in n8n do you find the list of past workflow runs?**
option.1: The sticky note on the canvas
option.2: The credential screen for logins
option.3: The Executions list in the menu
option.4: The Tidy Up control on the canvas
answerExplanation: Executions lists each run with its status.

contentBody: **What does a credential store for your nodes?**
option.1: A saved, secure login to an outside app
option.2: A form field and its label on the page
option.3: A schedule for when the workflow should run
option.4: A small sample of test data
answerExplanation: Nodes reuse the credential to connect to the app.

contentBody: **Are the keys Email and email treated the same in JSON data?**
option.1: Yes, they are always identical
option.2: Only when shown in the Table view
option.3: Only when they come from form data
option.4: No, since JSON keys are case-sensitive
answerExplanation: A wrong capital letter in an expression returns nothing.

contentBody: **Which trigger node would best fit "run every Monday at 9 am"?**
option.1: The "On form submission" trigger
option.2: The "On a schedule" trigger
option.3: The "On webhook call" trigger
option.4: The "Trigger manually" option
answerExplanation: A schedule trigger starts the workflow at a set time.

contentBody: **A form trigger's Test URL works only when...**
option.1: The workflow has been published already
option.2: The Google Sheet is completely empty
option.3: It is during working hours
option.4: You are listening for a test event right now
answerExplanation: The Production URL needs Publish; the Test URL needs the editor listening.

contentBody: **Matching the form's Email field to the sheet's Email column in a node is called...**
option.1: Publishing the workflow
option.2: Pinning the data
option.3: Mapping the fields
option.4: Tidying the canvas
answerExplanation: Mapping tells the action node which data goes in which column.

contentBody: **A published workflow ran, but the editor shows nothing new. Where should you look?**
option.1: The Executions list in n8n
option.2: The sticky note on the canvas
option.3: The form's Test URL page
option.4: The Help menu in the sidebar
answerExplanation: Production runs appear only in Executions.

contentBody: **Which of these proves the run really worked?**
option.1: The workflow's name shown at the top of the editor
option.2: Succeeded in n8n and the right row in the sheet
option.3: A green zoom button shown on the screen
option.4: The form page loading properly in a web browser
answerExplanation: Verify in both tools: the execution status and the data itself.

contentBody: **Which URL starts working after you publish a form workflow?**
option.1: Only the Test URL, as before
option.2: Neither of the two URLs
option.3: The Google Sheet's own URL
option.4: The Production URL for the form
answerExplanation: Publishing registers the production address.

contentBody: **A sheet column stays empty with Map Automatically. What is the likely cause?**
option.1: The sheet has too many rows for n8n to handle
option.2: The form has too few fields to fill the sheet
option.3: Field names don't exactly match the column headers
option.4: n8n is currently offline for everyone in the class
answerExplanation: Automatic mapping matches by name, with no error when a name differs.

contentBody: **What should you do with a practice workflow when you have finished?**
option.1: Leave it published and running
option.2: Unpublish it, or delete it entirely
option.3: Share the form link widely with others
option.4: Add some real customer data
answerExplanation: A published form is open to anyone with the link.
